_note: Intra-East-Asian blend (Chinese + Japanese): a sinicized Sino-Japanese maritime kingdom (Ritsuryo/Ryukyu-flavored) of the dragon-throne (Ryujin = dragon-god; homeland Ryujo). Backbone = Japonic (phonology, clan structure); overlay = Sinitic (Chinese-model bureaucracy, on'yomi court titles, the tributary system). civ = feudal. Even split Lawful/Neutral. SYNCRETIC religion (honji-suijaku): honors BOTH the Chinese celestial powers (Sinitic names) and the native kami (Japonic names) as one power under two faces. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Sino-Japanese/Ryukyuan register (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names draw on BOTH family_east_asian.json theonym sets, never real gods.

phonology.palette: Japonic base (open CV moras; vowels a i u e o; rendaku) with a heavy Sino-Japanese (on'yomi) overlay: Chinese loanwords read in Japanese phonology, a court/bureaucratic register; clan(-shi) + given.
phonology.phonotactics: strict CV moras, vowel-final; on'yomi compounds in the high register.

morphology.patronymic_form: clan/house name (-shi / ichizoku) first, then given; Sino-Japanese court titles; -no- linking; on'yomi style-names for officials and clergy.
morphology.compounding_rule: [clan] no [given]; toponyms feature/quality + type, often on'yomi: Dai-jo (great-castle), Ryu-to (dragon-capital), Kin-zan (gold-mountain).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a sinicized Sino-Japanese kingdom on the Chinese model: the Tei/O over a bureaucracy of court ranks, the dragon-throne; a maritime trading realm)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Sino-Japanese sinicized monarchy, ascending. The Tei (emperor; on'yomi of Chinese 'di') over the O (kings) and Shinno (royal princes); the bureaucracy of Bugyo (commissioner) and Kokushi (province-governor) on the Chinese/Ritsuryo model; the Aji are the local lords (Ryukyuan register); Sakimori guard the frontier. (Rank titles are the real Sino-Japanese/Ryukyuan register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: clan/house (-shi / ichizoku) first, then given; officials take a Sino-Japanese court rank; the cultured a Buddhist or studio name (-in/-an).
people_name_convention.dual_register: the court and bureaucracy use Sino-Japanese (on'yomi) names and titles; the common folk Japanese (kun'yomi) names.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names honor both the kami and the celestial powers + an element: Ryu- (dragon), -maru, Ten- (heaven, on'yomi): e.g. Ryutaro, Tenmaru, names blessing both Terashi-no-kami and Tuli-di.

religion._note: Ryujin is SYNCRETIC (the Sino-Japanese honji-suijaku BELIEF): the world HOLDS each power to be one being under two faces - a Chinese celestial official (Sinitic name) and a native kami (Japonic name). This is a belief, NOT a naming operation: the temple-namer never concatenates the two faces. Each holy site takes ONE name, chosen by its building type (see naming_rule), so naming costs exactly what a single-pantheon culture costs. Across a province the player sees the celestial face on Miao/Jiin halls and the kami face on Miya/Jinja shrines, and infers they are the same power - the syncretism surfaces through the spread of names, not within any one name. Faces draw on BOTH family_east_asian.json theonym sets; never real gods. Lawful/Neutral; the dragon-powers of sea and storm are especially honored (Ryujo, the dragon-realm).
religion.naming_rule: ONE name per holy site, selected by building type: a celestial hall (Miao, Jiin) takes the power's .celestial face; a kami-shrine (Miya, Jinja) takes its .kami face. The namer reads one field and formats '[building] of [face]' - identical cost to any single-pantheon culture. NEVER emit both faces in one name. The honji-suijaku identity (the two faces are one power) is surfaced in lore/dialogue text, not in proper names.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: ONE face per site by building type (see naming_rule): celestial hall -> 'the Jiin of Tuli-di', 'the Miao of Gaidun-di'; kami-shrine -> 'the Miya of Terashi-no-kami', 'the Jinja of Iwane-no-kami'. Both kinds occur across a realm; each name carries a single face.
religion.saints_pattern: deified sages, dragon-kings and ancestral heroes; named with the single face matching their site (celestial hall or kami-shrine).

holy_symbol_motifs.Tuli-di: a sun-disc above a coiled dragon and mirror (celestial face)
holy_symbol_motifs.Terashi-no-kami: a rising sun-disc above a mirror and sword (kami face)
holy_symbol_motifs.the dragon-powers: a sea-dragon encircling a flaming pearl

banks_patterns.ships: a maritime dragon-realm: trade-junk and dragon-prowed ship names: 'the Dragon-Pearl', 'Wave-Sovereign', 'the Ten-thousand-li Wind'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [clan] Gun / the [color] Banner: 'the Azure-Dragon Banner', 'the Pearl Guard'
banks_patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]': 'The Dragon and Pearl', 'The Jade Wave Teahouse'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: sunken sea-shrines and ruined dragon-jo: 'the Sunken Miya of [name]', 'the Dragon-tomb of [O]'
